title: Pricing a Return Credit where the Delivery Cannot Be Told Apart, Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
Questions answered on the unit price a returned crop protection line is credited at on an account of the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, where the account's own records leave the delivery in doubt.

**The member has been drawing on prepay this season. What price is the credit computed at?** Where a drawdown against a prepay booking stands on the account over the 10 statement months before the handling date, the credit is computed at the price the most recent prepay booking on the account locked. The most recent booking is the most recent prepay booking standing on the account, whatever product it named.

**No prepay has been drawn, but crop protection has come off the plant several times. What then?** Where no drawdown against a prepay booking stands on the account over those months and more than one crop protection delivery has been invoiced on the account over those months, the cooperative cannot tell which of those deliveries the product came off and credits the member at the dearest of them, so the credit is computed at the highest unit price at which crop protection has ever been invoiced on the account.

**Over what period is that highest price looked for?** Over the whole life of the account, not only over the 10 statement months; it is the count of crop protection deliveries that is taken over those months.

**No prepay drawn and only one crop protection delivery on the account inside the window.** Then no substituted price is used, and the credit is computed at no price other than the one the record already gives for the line coming back.
